newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: U.S., Japan, S.Korea to hold talks on N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S., Japan, S.Korea to hold talks on N.Korea.

text.p: The United States, Japan and South Korea will hold talks next week to coordinate policies on troubled North Korea, a South Korean foreign ministry spokesman said on Friday.
The meeting in Tokyo on Wednesday will focus on food shortages in the North and ways to encourage the Stalinist nation to join peace talks, Lee Kyu-hyung said.
It will be led by Charles Kartman, U.S. deputy assistant secretary of state, Yu Myung-hwan, a director-general at the South Korean foreign ministry, and his Japanese counterpart, Ryozo Kato.
North Korea last month agreed to join four-nation peace talks if it was first guaranteed large-scale food aid, U.S. diplomatic recognition and an easing of trade sanctions.
Peace talks involving the two Koreas, the United States and China, are aimed at closing the book on the 1950-53 Korean War, which ended in a now-fraying armistice.
Lee said Seoul and its allies agreed Pyongyang must not be allow to use participation in the four-way talks as leverage to extract food assistance.
Washington and Seoul have said substantial aid could be discussed during peace talks, although humanitarian assistance would be provided to help stave off a catastrophe.

The United States has pledged $25 million and South Korea $6 million to the World Food Programme, which has appealed for $95.5 million to provide 203,000 tonnes of food to North Korea. A Seoul official said South Korea was considering sending an additional 50,000 tonnes of corn.
Japan has held back food aid, partly due to anger over charges that North Korea kidnapped a Japanese schoolgirl in 1977 and spirited her to Pyongyang.
Officials in Seoul, Tokyo and Washington worry that a desperate North Korean leadership might strike the South if an economic crisis threatened its survival.

Last month, Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda told parliament there were unconfirmed reports that North Korea may have deployed Rodong-1 ballistic missiles, capable of hitting all parts of Japan.
